idea: Faceless illustrated mini-documentaries on the hidden engineering, design decisions and strange history of everyday things (The Curious Mechanism playbook).
audience: Global, English-speaking, 18-44, curious adults who watch engineering, design and history explainers
promise: one everyday object, one question, the hidden engineering behind it
notes: Source: the-curious-mechanism.zip playbook (PLAYBOOK.md, brand/style-guide.md). Niche leaders (Half as Interesting, Practical Engineering, Jared Owen, Steve Mould, Primal Space) share: a question-title (Why/How), a 15-20 s hook with no intro, one clean diagram look, 8-15 min long-form plus Shorts cut from it. Gap: none uses a 19th-century engraving / patent-drawing look; that is the brand. Long-form 8-12 min weekly on YouTube; 2-3 Shorts a week (30-55 s, 9:16, complete mini-story) on every platform. Brand font is Libre Baskerville (Google Fonts); kit uses DejaVu Serif because kit.py renders with locally installed fonts. Handle 'curiousmechanism' is 16 chars, over the 15-char X limit, so handles are shortened.

names.why: Playbook name kept; ai suffix says AI-made up front; 13 chars fits X.
Closest to the full name; 14 chars; AI disclosure stays in the bio.
Shortest, easiest to spell after hearing it once.

style.look: 19th-century engineering encyclopedia illustration: detailed hand-engraved ink drawing on antique ivory paper, fine cross-hatching and precise linework, muted navy blue and charcoal ink with an occasional muted red accent and brass tones on metal parts, subtle vintage paper imperfections, scientifically plausible proportions, museum-quality technical drawing, clear central subject, calm and curious mood. No photography, no photorealism, no cartoon characters, no labels or text in the image.
style.avatar_subject: a single engraved brass gear seen through a round magnifying glass, ink blue linework on antique ivory paper, centered, no text
style.banner_scene: a wide engraved encyclopedia plate on antique ivory paper: in the centre band, a cutaway of a ballpoint pen, an airplane window and a pocket-watch gear train side by side; calm empty paper towards the edges
style.banner_line: the hidden engineering of everyday things

youtube.name: The Curious Mechanism
youtube.description:
Welcome to The Curious Mechanism.

Every video answers one question about an everyday thing: why airplane windows are round, what is inside a ballpoint pen, how GPS knows where you are. We look at the hidden engineering, the design decisions and the strange history behind ordinary objects.

How it's made: every topic is researched from at least two reliable sources, listed in each description. Illustrations and narration are made with AI tools; research, script and editing are done by a person.

A new mini-documentary every week, Shorts in between.

Nothing is ordinary when you understand how it works. Tell us in the comments which everyday object we should open up next.
